4: /**
5:  * Content library seed data, ported verbatim from design/_shared/library.js.
6:  * Everything here is a *definition*; character sheets reference these by Id and never copy
7:  * them, so an admin-panel edit reaches every sheet on next render.
8:  */

10: /** Bump this whenever the content returned by `seedLibrary()` below changes. `runSeedIfEmpty()`
11:  *  only seeds an empty database, so a live library never picks up a seed edit on its own — the
12:  *  live library staying 16 releases stale went undetected for months (HANDOFF.md open issue 19).
13:  *  This gets stamped onto every seeded/reset `Library.SeedVersion`, so the live row can be compared
14:  *  against this constant to detect that drift automatically instead of relying on someone
15:  *  remembering to diff the two by hand. Any string works; matching the app version this content
16:  *  last changed in keeps it self-documenting. */
17: export const SEED_VERSION = '0.63.0';
18:

22:  *  category) — kept as two distinct trees with the same display Name, disambiguated by Category,
23:  *  rather than merged into one. */

52: const SEED_IMPROVEMENT_TREES: ImprovementTree[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.map((t) => ({ Id: t.id, Name: t.name, Category: t.category, Description: t.description }));
53: 
54: /** Ruleset-V0.5.md names all 25 trees above but never authors a single node on any of them — no
55:  *  Starting Improvement, no prerequisite line, nothing (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12). Rather
56:  *  than invent real mechanical effects that don't exist in the source document, each tree gets
57:  *  exactly two clearly-labeled placeholder nodes (a Starting Improvement and one node chained to
58:  *  it) — enough to exercise the DAG gate (`improvementState` in `logic.ts`) and the admin
59:  *  validation (`validateImprovementDag` in `adminLogic.ts`) end to end. Replace these with real
60:  *  authored content once the repo owner writes it; nothing else in this slice depends on their
61:  *  Effect text being real. */
62: const PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT = 'Placeholder — Ruleset-V0.5.md names this tree but has not authored its Improvements yet. This node only exists to exercise the prerequisite DAG; replace with real content (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12).';
63: 
64: const SEED_IMPROVEMENTS: Improvement[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.flatMap((t) => {
65:   const startId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-1`;
66:   const nextId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-2`;
67:   return [
68:     { Id: startId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} I (Starting, placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: true, PrerequisiteIds: [] },
69:     { Id: nextId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} II (placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: false, PrerequisiteIds: [startId] },
70:   ];
71: });

import type { Improvement, ImprovementTree, Library } from './types.js';
import { GM_REFERENCE } from './seedGmReference.js';

/**
 * Content library seed data, ported verbatim from design/_shared/library.js.
 * Everything here is a *definition*; character sheets reference these by Id and never copy
 * them, so an admin-panel edit reaches every sheet on next render.
 */

/** Bump this whenever the content returned by `seedLibrary()` below changes. `runSeedIfEmpty()`
 *  only seeds an empty database, so a live library never picks up a seed edit on its own — the
 *  live library staying 16 releases stale went undetected for months (HANDOFF.md open issue 19).
 *  This gets stamped onto every seeded/reset `Library.SeedVersion`, so the live row can be compared
 *  against this constant to detect that drift automatically instead of relying on someone
 *  remembering to diff the two by hand. Any string works; matching the app version this content
 *  last changed in keeps it self-documenting. */
export const SEED_VERSION = '0.63.0';

/** The 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat + 14 Narrative), named and themed directly from
 *  Ruleset-V0.5.md's "Hero Improvements" section — real, authored content, unlike the
 *  placeholder nodes built on top of them below. "Command" is named twice in the doc (once per
 *  category) — kept as two distinct trees with the same display Name, disambiguated by Category,
 *  rather than merged into one. */
const IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS: { id: string; name: string; category: 'Combat' | 'Narrative'; description: string }[] = [
  { id: 'it-strike', name: 'Strike', category: 'Combat', description: 'Direct attacks, signature weapons, and straightforward harm.' },
  { id: 'it-smash', name: 'Smash', category: 'Combat', description: 'Overwhelming force, wide destruction, and broken obstacles.' },
  { id: 'it-exploit', name: 'Exploit', category: 'Combat', description: 'Ambushes, marks, counters, and weak points.' },
  { id: 'it-control', name: 'Control', category: 'Combat', description: 'Restraint, forced movement, fear, terrain, and denial.' },
  { id: 'it-maneuver', name: 'Maneuver', category: 'Combat', description: 'Charges, retreats, leaps, flight, teleportation, and repositioning.' },
  { id: 'it-guard', name: 'Guard', category: 'Combat', description: 'Armor, shields, wards, parries, and interposition.' },
  { id: 'it-endure', name: 'Endure', category: 'Combat', description: 'Durability, resistance, recovery, and refusing defeat.' },
  { id: 'it-support', name: 'Support', category: 'Combat', description: 'Healing, cleansing, empowerment, and practical aid.' },
  { id: 'it-command-combat', name: 'Command', category: 'Combat', description: 'Formations, morale, coordination, and directing allies.' },

const SEED_IMPROVEMENT_TREES: ImprovementTree[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.map((t) => ({ Id: t.id, Name: t.name, Category: t.category, Description: t.description }));

/** Ruleset-V0.5.md names all 25 trees above but never authors a single node on any of them — no
 *  Starting Improvement, no prerequisite line, nothing (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12). Rather
 *  than invent real mechanical effects that don't exist in the source document, each tree gets
 *  exactly two clearly-labeled placeholder nodes (a Starting Improvement and one node chained to
 *  it) — enough to exercise the DAG gate (`improvementState` in `logic.ts`) and the admin
 *  validation (`validateImprovementDag` in `adminLogic.ts`) end to end. Replace these with real
 *  authored content once the repo owner writes it; nothing else in this slice depends on their
 *  Effect text being real. */
const PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT = 'Placeholder — Ruleset-V0.5.md names this tree but has not authored its Improvements yet. This node only exists to exercise the prerequisite DAG; replace with real content (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12).';

const SEED_IMPROVEMENTS: Improvement[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.flatMap((t) => {
  const startId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-1`;
  const nextId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-2`;
  return [
    { Id: startId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} I (Starting, placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: true, PrerequisiteIds: [] },
    { Id: nextId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} II (placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: false, PrerequisiteIds: [startId] },
  ];
});

5:  * GM-tooling import format. Keep them stable; add fields rather than renaming.
6:  */

8: // ---------- Content Library (authored in the admin panel, read-only to players) ----------

45: /** A Motif is the core aspect of a Hero — one of three per character, replacing the single Theme
46:  *  of the pre-V0.5 ruleset. Each Motif is a bucket for that Hero's Skill Tags, Flaw Tags, its own
47:  *  Potential track, and a Quest. Players choose from the 13 canonical Motifs (or write their own)
48:  *  and may rename any of them to fit their character's flavor. */
49: export interface Motif {
50:   Id: string;
51:   Name: string;
52:   Description: string;

54:   FlawTagExamples: string[];

57: /** V0.5's authored Hero Improvements: 11 Combat + 14 Narrative trees (Ruleset-V0.5.md, "Hero
58:  *  Improvements"). `library.improvementTrees` names and themes them; `library.improvements`
59:  *  holds their actual nodes. Party and Bond get an "Improvement" mention too (the doc's own
60:  *  "Party Motif + Improvements"/"Bond Track + Improvements" headers), but neither names any
61:  *  trees at all — both sections read "Here that is!" with nothing under them — so this slice
62:  *  only builds the Hero side; see HANDOFF.md open issue 12 for the gap. */
63: export type ImprovementCategory = 'Combat' | 'Narrative';
64:

66:   Id: string;
67:   Name: string;
68:   Category: ImprovementCategory;
69:   Description: string;
70: }

72: /** One node on an Improvement Tree, replacing the flat Tier-gated `Advancement` list (slice 4).
73:  *  Gating is DAG-only, per Ruleset-V0.5.md's own current rule (lines 458/489): take a Starting
74:  *  Improvement on any tree, or one connected to an Improvement you already hold on that same
75:  *  tree; each takeable once. The doc's separate "Level Up"/"Progress the Party" section names a
76:  *  Tier-1..4-and-Level gate instead — read as leftover text from an earlier, unreconciled draft
77:  *  (it pastes the old flat-list gate onto the newer tree model, and nowhere else in the doc
78:  *  assigns a Tier to a tree node) and deliberately not implemented; confirmed with the repo
79:  *  owner rather than guessed — see HANDOFF.md open issue 12. `PrerequisiteIds` only ever names
80:  *  other Improvements on the same `TreeId`; nothing here validates that at the type level, but
81:  *  `apps/server/src/adminLogic.ts`'s `validateLibrary` does. */
82: export interface Improvement {
83:   Id: string;
84:   TreeId: string;
85:   Name: string;
86:   Effect: string;
87:   IsStarting: boolean;
88:   PrerequisiteIds: string[];
89: }

105: export interface Move {

107:   Name: string;
108:   Kind: MoveKind;
109:   VirtueId: string | null;
110:   Description: string;
111:   Results: MoveResults;
112:   PlayerVariantResults?: MoveResults | null;
113:   /** Hold this Move grants directly on a reported roll tier (V0.5 slice 3) — e.g. Assess the
114:    *  Situation grants 3 on a 10+. Only the two Moves whose Hold grant is a literal number carry
115:    *  this; every other Move's Tier results stay freeform reference text with no mechanical hook.
116:    *  Missing/omitted for a tier means that tier grants no Hold. See `holdGrantForTier()`
117:    *  (`engine.ts`) for how this is applied once a player reports which tier they hit. */
118:   HoldGrant?: Partial<Record<'Tier3' | 'Tier2' | 'Tier1', number>>;

121: /** A rules term or phrase whose definition should be reachable as an inline tap-link anywhere it
122:  *  appears in authored text (move/skill/ability descriptions, etc.) — see `glossary.ts`'s
123:  *  `buildGlossaryMatcher`/`linkifyText`. Deliberately its own collection rather than borrowing
124:  *  `Description`-shaped fields off existing entities: general mechanics referenced in prose
125:  *  ("Condition", "Bond", "Hold") often have no single matching entity — `conditions` holds five
126:  *  specific per-Virtue Conditions, not the mechanic itself. `Name` doubles as the canonical
127:  *  matched phrase; `Aliases` covers other forms (plurals, "Mark Bond" vs "Bond") that should link
128:  *  to the same definition without duplicating it. */
129: export interface GlossaryTerm {
130:   Id: string;
131:   Name: string;
132:   Aliases: string[];
133:   Definition: string;
134: }

158:   SevereStatusSlots: number;
159:   /** Library-wide kill switch for the regex auto-linker in `glossary.ts` (0.24.0). Defaults

161:    *  least one explicit `[Term]` tag always disables auto-linking for that one field regardless
162:    *  of this setting; this flag is for retiring the regex matcher library-wide once content has
163:    *  fully migrated to explicit tags. */
164:   GlossaryAutoLink: boolean;

383: /** A GM-authored Adventure (Ruleset-V0.5.md's "Adventures" chapter — the fourth surface, alongside

385:  *  content — unlike `Villain`/`NPC`/`Location` (slice 8, shared authored stat blocks any campaign
386:  *  could reuse), an Adventure is one GM's specific combination of those for one specific campaign,
387:  *  so it lives alongside `Encounter`/`Clock` rather than in `Library`. `VillainId`/`NpcIds`/
388:  *  `LocationIds` are `Ref`s into the campaign's shared `library.villains`/`npcs`/`locations` —
389:  *  the doc's own "an Adventure references them, it does not redefine them" framing (WorkPlan-V0.5.md

391:  *  `Concluded`) since a campaign may run several Adventures over its life — "the start of a new
392:  *  Adventure!" once a Villain's Goal is thwarted — the same "no single active row" shape `Clock`
393:  *  already established, not Combat's "one Active Encounter" shape. GM-authored and GM-only to write
394:  *  (unlike a Clock, which any campaign member may progress) — see CLAUDE.md's "Architecture:
395:  *  Adventures" for why this stays GM-only end to end rather than gaining a partial player-facing
396:  *  view. */
397: export interface Adventure {
398:   Id: string;
399:   CampaignId: string;
400:   Concept: string;

402:   Hook: string;
403:   VillainId: string | null;
404:   NpcIds: string[];
405:   LocationIds: string[];
406:   Secrets: AdventureSecret[];

409:    *  reached). "A Countdown is a clock variant" (WorkPlan-V0.5.md slice 9 scope) — this reuses
410:    *  `Clock`'s own tick-and-clamp mechanic (`tickAdventureCountdown()` in `adventures.ts`, the same
411:    *  clamped-delta shape as `clocks.ts`'s `tickClock()`) rather than the `Clock` type itself.
412:    *  A real linked `Clock` row was the first design tried and deliberately dropped: every other
413:    *  Clock in this app is fully player-visible (ClocksPanel, Realtime-synced), but an Adventure's
414:    *  own Countdown is explicitly the GM's off-screen reference ("what is happening with the
415:    *  Villain when they are off-screen") — the doc's own distinction from a *Threat* (also
416:    *  Countdown-kind, but "player facing"), which stays a real, separately-created `Clock` reached
417:    *  through ClocksPanel as always. Embedding the count directly here keeps it inside the same
418:    *  GM-only boundary as the rest of the Adventure (never fetched for a Player, never Realtime-
419:    *  synced) with no new field-level access control needed — see CLAUDE.md's "Architecture:
420:    *  Adventures". */
421:   CountdownMarks: number;
422:   Status: 'Active' | 'Concluded';
423:   CreatedAt: string;
424:   UpdatedAt: string;
425: }

429: /** Step 1 of the five-step collaborative map build ("Where the Adventure Begins") —
430:  *  `Ruleset-V0.6.md`'s "Creating the World" chapter, adapted from *The Perilous Wilds*. One
431:  *  starting place per campaign, not a list — every later step (Regions, Places of Interest, ...)
432:  *  builds outward from it. `Details` is one freeform entry per player introducing a local-area
433:  *  detail ("a mysterious lighthouse, a thick forest..."); the seven scalar fields are the doc's
434:  *  own fixed prompts, asked in order, each a short freeform answer rather than a pick from a
435:  *  list — the doc gives illustrative examples ("prospering, floundering, etc.", "amicable,
436:  *  competitive, envious, charitable, etc.") for two of them, not an exhaustive set. `Rumors` is
437:  *  this step's own "each player shares one rumor about the place where the party will start" —

439:  *  doc frames them as two different prompts, not one list asked twice. */

458:  *  rumor about that region... but don't feel pressure to." */

500: /** Shared campaign world-building content — `Ruleset-V0.6.md`'s new "Creating the World" chapter
501:  *  (V0.6 slice 8, `WorkPlan-V0.6.md` Section C's Slice 8 bullet), CATS plus a five-step
502:  *  collaborative map build adapted from *The Perilous Wilds*. One row per campaign, the same
503:  *  "single shared JSONB blob" shape `Party` already established, since this is exactly that kind
504:  *  of content: collaboratively written, visible to and editable by the whole table at once, not
505:  *  authored library content and not one player's own sheet.
506:  *
507:  *  **CATS** (`Concept`/`Aim`/`Tone`/`SubjectMatter`) is a short one-time group discussion, not a
508:  *  mechanic — captured here as four freeform notes so the table has a durable record of what was
509:  *  agreed, not because the app enforces any of it.
510:  *
511:  *  **The five-step map build is genuinely six sections in the source text, not five — a real doc
512:  *  inconsistency, carried forward rather than silently fixed, the same discipline this app already
513:  *  applies to the Adventure Countdown's "five steps, prose promises six."** The chapter's own
514:  *  headers are "Step 1: Where the Adventure Begins," "Step 2: The Surrounding Regions," "Step 2:
515:  *  Places of Interest" (reusing "Step 2" a second time — a numbering slip, not a merged step; the
516:  *  two sections' own instructions are clearly sequential, "Now, starting with the player whose
517:  *  character is the most traveled..."), "Step 3: Personal Places," "Step 4: Create Connectors,"
518:  *  and "Step 5: Start Rumors." `WorkPlan-V0.6.md`'s own paraphrase ("starting place and its
519:  *  questions, surrounding regions, places of interest, personal places, connectors, opening
520:  *  rumors") lists all six while still calling it "five-step" — this app ships all six sections
521:  *  exactly as headed, and documents the mismatch rather than merging or dropping one to make the
522:  *  count match.
523:  *
524:  *  **World-building happens before character creation in this app, reversing the doc's own
525:  *  narrated order.** The chapter's prose has World-building follow Character Creation ("After
526:  *  you've done this, go ahead and create your characters... Now it is time to place them in a
527:  *  setting"), but `WorkPlan-V0.6.md`'s own Slice 8 scope calls this "a campaign Signup-phase
528:  *  surface" — and this app's `Campaign.Phase` model already reserves character creation for
529:  *  `PartyCreation`, the phase *after* Signup. Rather than reopen that phase ordering, World stays
530:  *  reachable (not phase-gated at all — see `apps/server/src/routes/world.ts`) for the life of the
531:  *  campaign, matching the doc's own "you don't need to know everything right now... you can add
532:  *  more of any of them as your adventure plays out." `PersonalPlace` is the one section this
533:  *  ordering change actually touches: see its own doc comment. */

535:   Id: string;
536:   CampaignId: string;
537:   Concept: string;
538:   Aim: string;
539:   Tone: string;
540:   SubjectMatter: string;
541:   StartingPlace: StartingPlace;
542:   Regions: WorldRegion[];
543:   PlacesOfInterest: PlaceOfInterest[];
544:   PersonalPlaces: PersonalPlace[];
545:   Connectors: Connector[];

548:   Rumors: string[];

550:   UpdatedBy: string | null;

149:     glossary: [
150:       { Id: 'g-condition', Name: 'Condition', Aliases: ['Conditions'], Definition: 'A marked penalty tied to one of your five Virtues — Exhausted (Might), Afraid (Mettle), Guilty (Heart), Angry (Wit), Insecure (Guile). When you mark a Condition, you gain an associated Bane on any relevant roll until you clear it. Marking a Condition when all five are already marked means you Crumble.' },
151:       { Id: 'g-hero-roll', Name: 'Hero Roll', Aliases: ['Hero Rolls'], Definition: 'Roll 2d6 and add the relevant Virtue. Add +1 for one relevant Skill Tag and −1 for every relevant Flaw Tag. You may Push Yourself once per roll: mark a Condition and add +1 for a second relevant Skill Tag. The final modifier cannot exceed +3 or fall below −3. After determining the modifier, apply Advantage or Disadvantage from your Boons and Banes.' },
152:       { Id: 'g-misfortune', Name: 'Misfortune', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The GM’s currency. At the beginning of a Session, if the GM has none, they gain 1. Whenever a Hero rolls 6-, in or out of Combat, the GM gains 1. The GM spends it 1 for 1 to make a Hard Move at any time, including immediately, and some GM and Enemy Moves cost Misfortune too. It carries over between Sessions and resets to 1 when an Adventure concludes.' },
153:       { Id: 'g-hard-move', Name: 'Hard Move', Aliases: ['Hard Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that gives the Heroes no time to react: it afflicts them with a tangible penalty, in the fiction or directly (marking Strain or a Condition), and the stakes meaningfully change. The GM must spend a Misfortune to make one.' },
154:       { Id: 'g-soft-move', Name: 'Soft Move', Aliases: ['Soft Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that threatens danger or pushes the Heroes toward a choice, while leaving them time to stop or divert it — often a setup ending in “What do you do?” A Soft Move can telegraph a later Hard Move.' },
155:       { Id: 'g-rapport', Name: 'Rapport', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A party-wide track marked when a move tells you to "mark Rapport." Filling it clears the track and raises Party Level by 1 — see Improvement. Rapport can also be spent directly as Aid — see Aid.' },
156:       { Id: 'g-work-together', Name: 'Work Together', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When any number of Heroes want to work as a group, the GM may ask for the Party to make a single Hero Roll to determine the outcome of a Move where the Party is acting as one. Each Hero may contribute one relevant Skill Tag, and any or all of the Party Tags may be used if they are relevant. All Hero’s Flaw Tags may affect the roll as well, and the outcome affects the entire group.' },
157:       { Id: 'g-party-quest', Name: 'Party Quest', Aliases: ['Party Quests'], Definition: 'What your group all must seek together — your reason for traveling as one rather than individuals. It creates a path forward leading into Adventures and drives the story. Four varieties help define it: Vision (how the Party wants to change their world), Covenant (a binding vow or shared ideology), Shield (a realm or population to defend), or Expedition (a mystery or truth to uncover).' },
158:       { Id: 'g-motif', Name: 'Motif', Aliases: ['Motifs'], Definition: 'One of the three core aspects of your Hero — each a bucket for its own Skill Tags, Flaw Tags, a Potential track, and a Quest. You choose three Motifs at creation (from the thirteen suggested, or your own) and may rename any of them to fit your character.' },
159:       { Id: 'g-skill-tag', Name: 'Skill Tag', Aliases: ['Skill Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing something your Hero is good at. Declare a relevant Skill Tag before a roll to add +1; if more than one applies you may Push Yourself, mark a Condition, and add another +1.' },
160:       { Id: 'g-flaw-tag', Name: 'Flaw Tag', Aliases: ['Flaw Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing a limit or weakness. A relevant Flaw Tag gives -1 to the roll, and acting on it marks Potential on that Motif whether the roll succeeds or fails.' },
161:       { Id: 'g-quest', Name: 'Quest', Aliases: ['Quests'], Definition: 'A short, player-written goal hanging off one Motif, tracked with three Act Breaks and three Forsakes. Three Act Breaks complete it; three Forsakes abandon it.' },
162:       { Id: 'g-potential', Name: 'Potential', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A track on each Motif, marked when a move tells you to "mark Potential" (or when you act on a Flaw Tag). Filling a Motif’s track clears it, raises Level by 1, and lets you add a Skill Tag, add or remove a Flaw Tag, or gain a Hero Improvement — see Improvement.' },
163:       { Id: 'g-improvement', Name: 'Improvement', Aliases: ['Improvements', 'Improvement Tree', 'Hero Improvement'], Definition: 'A permanent pick taken off one of 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat, 14 Narrative) when a full Motif Potential track clears. Each tree is its own small prerequisite chain: take a tree’s Starting Improvement any time, or any other Improvement on that tree once you already hold one it connects to. Each Improvement can only be taken once. Party Improvements are named in the rules the same way but have no authored trees yet.' },
164:       { Id: 'g-hold', Name: 'Hold', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A pool of uses granted by a Move on a strong hit and spent one at a time until it runs out. Assess the Situation and Discern the Truth grant it; spend it to refresh a piece of Gear, clear a Condition, mark a Bond, or mark Potential.' },
165:       { Id: 'g-load', Name: 'Load', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How much you can carry. Each Item has a Load cost (0, 1, or 2); your total carried Load is capped by your Light/Normal/Heavy tier.' },
166:       { Id: 'g-bond', Name: 'Bond', Aliases: ['Bonds', 'Mark Bond', 'Bond Track', 'Bond Level'], Definition: 'How deeply a Connection between two Heroes runs, measured on its Bond Track. Mark 1 Bond when your Connection Tag meaningfully influences an important choice, creates a significant complication, or helps the two of you overcome a great obstacle together (once per Connection per scene), or when a move tells you to "mark Bond". At 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the Bond Track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement. Either Hero may spend a Bond at any time to influence the other. Marking Bond and Forging go through a propose/accept/reject handshake between the two players; spending Bond applies immediately.' },
167:       { Id: 'g-connection', Name: 'Connection', Aliases: ['Connections', 'Connection Tag', 'Connection Tags'], Definition: "Each pair of Heroes has one Connection, with a Connection Tag the two agree on that describes where their relationship stands now — pick one of the ruleset's examples or write your own. Bond is marked on it; at 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement." },
168:       { Id: 'g-status', Name: 'Status', Aliases: ['Statuses'], Definition: 'A named, lasting injury held in one of three severity slots — Minor (×3), Major (×2), or Severe (×1). Only the highest-severity Status you hold ever penalizes a roll: Minor is −1, Major is Disadvantage, Severe means rolling 1d6 instead of 2d6. Distinct from Strain (a short-term track that clears at the end of a scene) and from a Condition (always one of the five Virtue-linked penalties). Reduced by Recuperating, or downgraded a severity when your Healing Track fills.' },
169:       { Id: 'g-strain', Name: 'Strain', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-box short-term harm track that clears completely at the end of the scene or Combat in which it was taken. Mark the box equal to an incoming amount, or the next unmarked box to its right. Resist an incoming amount by rolling + a Virtue to reduce it, or by choosing to take a Status instead (which absorbs a flat 2/4/6 by severity). Armor negates Strain entirely, up to its own limit.' },
170:       { Id: 'g-healing-track', Name: 'Healing Track', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-segment track advanced by Recuperating (+Mettle: 3/2/1 segments by tier). When it fills, every Status you hold drops one severity (renamed to reflect the improvement, where a slot is free at the lower severity) and the track clears, carrying any remaining segments onto the fresh one.' },
171:       { Id: 'g-boon', Name: 'Boon', Aliases: ['Boons'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working in your favor — cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Banes on a roll: more relevant Boons than Banes gives Advantage. See Advantage.' },
172:       { Id: 'g-bane', Name: 'Bane', Aliases: ['Banes'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working against you — cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Boons on a roll: more relevant Banes than Boons gives Disadvantage. See Advantage.' },
173:       { Id: 'g-immobilized', Name: 'Immobilized', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A special Bane representing anything that prevents voluntary movement: grappling, paralysis, restraints, or binding magic. While Immobilized your Speed is 0 and you cannot move voluntarily, Maneuver, or Shift, but you may take other actions and forced movement can still move you. A Boon may cancel its effect on a roll but does not restore your movement. It ends when its fictional cause disappears or when someone successfully uses Break.' },
174:       { Id: 'g-crumble', Name: 'Crumble', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When you need to mark a Condition but all of them are already marked, you Crumble: you lose consciousness, flee, or otherwise must leave the scene. Say how, then clear one Condition immediately, and discuss with the GM how and when you’ll return. If you Crumble in Combat, you can only take actions that result in you fleeing or avoiding the action.' },
175:       { Id: 'g-subdued', Name: 'Subdued', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When a Hero must mark Strain but has no Strain box and does not prevent the Strain by taking a Status or using Armor, they are Subdued: they cannot continue the conflict, and the player and GM describe how they are removed from immediate danger — knocked unconscious, pinned, captured, separated, or forced to retreat. Subdual does not kill a Hero unless the player agrees that death is the appropriate outcome; what else happens is left to the table. An Enemy is Subdued when no legal Strain box remains (a Minion by any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain), and the Hero who subdued it and the fiction decide whether it is unconscious, captured, routed, or killed.' },
176:       { Id: 'g-scar', Name: 'Scar', Aliases: ['Scars'], Definition: 'A near-permanent consequence a Hero can carry — a lost limb, a lingering nightmare, an unwanted transformation. The old Subdued-triggered choice that used to grant one (Take a Scar / Risk Death / Blaze of Glory) has been retired with no stated replacement; Scars themselves stay on the sheet as free text for whenever the table narrates one.' },
177:       { Id: 'g-guard', Name: 'Guard', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Reduces the Strain inflicted on an Enemy by its value — Guard 1 by 1, Guard 2 by 2 — but never below 1 Strain, and it doesn’t reduce Conditions or effects inflicted instead of Strain. Pierce ignores it. Guard should be visible in the fiction: a shield, a stone shell, a spectral barrier, impossible speed.' },
178:       { Id: 'g-pierce', Name: 'Pierce', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Gambit: ignore the Enemy’s Guard for this Move. See Guard.' },
179:       { Id: 'g-threat', Name: 'Threat', Aliases: ['Threat Level'], Definition: 'How many Heroes an Enemy is expected to occupy: ½ for a Minion, 1 Standard, 2 Elite, 4 Legendary. Add every Enemy’s Threat and divide by the number of Heroes — Easy .5, Medium .75, Hard 1, Deadly 1.25, Very Deadly 1.5 or more. It is only a starting estimate.' },
180:       { Id: 'g-enemy-profile', Name: 'Enemy Profile', Aliases: ['Enemy Profiles', 'Minion', 'Minions', 'Elite', 'Legendary'], Definition: 'How much of a fight an Enemy is, which sets its defaults for Strain, Status slots and Conditions. A Minion (Threat ½) is weak alone but dangerous in groups, and any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain Subdues it; a Standard Enemy (Threat 1) can take on one Hero; an Elite (Threat 2) can take on two at once; a Legendary Enemy (Threat 4) fights the whole party, taking a turn after every Hero’s turn. See Threat.' },
181:       { Id: 'g-last-stand', Name: 'Last Stand', Aliases: ['Bloodied'], Definition: 'A Legendary Enemy fights in three phases — Opening, Bloodied, then Last Stand (N) — each a five-box Strain track unless its stat block says otherwise. When a phase can’t mark incoming Strain, it ends and the rest of that Strain is discarded. It loses at most one phase between its own activations. Last Stand (N) clears the N highest-numbered marked boxes, which become its final capacity; when it can’t mark Strain in Last Stand, it is Subdued.' },
182:       { Id: 'g-range', Name: 'Range', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How far apart two combatants are: Melee, Close, Far, Very Far, or Out of Range. Maneuver and Shift move you between bands; Engage at Range and Engage in Melee each only work at their own band.' },
183:       { Id: 'g-aid', Name: 'Aid', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Spend 1 Rapport to give another Hero +1 on a roll, even after the dice are already rolled. You can Aid the same roll once per teammate, and Aid from multiple teammates stacks. Adding +1 this way cannot exceed +3 total on the roll.' },
184:       { Id: 'g-wealth', Name: 'Wealth', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet. Named sinks: spend 1 to roll Follow a Lead with Advantage, or during Enjoy Downtime to Rest, Carouse, Acquire, or Train.' },
185:       { Id: 'g-treasure', Name: 'Treasure', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet like Wealth. Ruleset-V0.6.md names no Wealth-distinct sink for Treasure any more — Carouse spends Wealth now — so it stays a freely adjusted resource with no automated hook.' },
186:       { Id: 'g-advantage', Name: 'Advantage', Aliases: ['Disadvantage'], Definition: 'Roll 3d6 and keep the best two (Advantage) or worst two (Disadvantage) instead of the usual 2d6 — decided by comparing your Boons and Banes relevant to the roll: more Boons is Advantage, more Banes is Disadvantage, a tie (including none of either) is Normal. A Major Status is a separate source of Disadvantage the ruleset doesn’t say how to combine with a Boon/Bane-driven one — both are shown, and the table resolves it. Double Disadvantage (from Repeated Attacks) is the worst possible roll: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two.' },
187:       { Id: 'g-double-disadvantage', Name: 'Double Disadvantage', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The worst possible roll a Hero can make, arising from Repeated Attacks: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two. This is the only rule that creates Double Disadvantage.' },
188:       { Id: 'g-repeated-attacks', Name: 'Repeated Attacks', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Whenever a Hero spends AP on a Move that can inflict Strain, count how many such Moves they have used since their AP last refreshed. Work out Advantage or Disadvantage from Boons and Banes as normal, then worsen the roll one step for each previous Strain-inflicting Move, as far as Double Disadvantage. A Move counts once however many creatures it targets, and a Reaction counts if it costs AP and can inflict Strain.' },
189:       { Id: 'g-prepare', Name: 'Prepare', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Combat Move: your maximum AP becomes 4 during your next turn. Prepare does not stack with itself, and after that turn ends your maximum returns to normal.' },
190:       { Id: 'g-combat-goal', Name: 'Combat Goal', Aliases: ['Combat Goals'], Definition: 'The objective that must be achieved to end Combat, agreed on by the GM and Heroes when entering the Combat system. Examples include defeating the opposition, rescuing a prisoner, recovering an item, crossing a bridge, or escaping an area. If the Heroes initiate Combat and all share the goal, they mark 1 Rapport.' },
191:       { Id: 'g-defiant-goal', Name: 'Defiant Goal', Aliases: ['Defiant Goals'], Definition: 'An alternative objective a minority of Heroes may declare during Combat if they disagree with the main Combat Goal. Achieving a Defiant Goal allows only those Heroes to leave Combat. Combat ends for everyone only if the table agrees the Defiant Goal has superseded the main Goal.' },
192:       { Id: 'g-consequence', Name: 'Consequence', Aliases: ['Burdened', 'Compromised', 'Delayed', 'Depleted', 'Exposed', 'Consequences'], Definition: 'One of five named outcomes on Invoke Expertise and Take a Risk: Burdened (a worse outcome, hard choice, or price to pay), Compromised (the situation escalates), Delayed (you take too long; things change meaningfully), Depleted (expend a resource or break a useful item), or Exposed (draw unwanted attention or leave a traceable trail). Replaces the old Attrition/Detection/Danger/Delay/Sacrifice vocabulary.' },
193:       { Id: 'g-camp-asset', Name: 'Camp Asset', Aliases: ['Camp Assets'], Definition: 'A magic item the party is afforded at creation to help them set up camp, leveling up through Tiers as the party progresses. Pick one from the library, or write your own on the spot.' },
194:       { Id: 'g-camp-action', Name: 'Camp Action', Aliases: ['Camp Actions'], Definition: 'One of the things each Hero may do at Make Camp: rewrite or update one of your Skill or Flaw Tags for the Party Motif, or for one of your Motifs; rewrite your Connection Tag, if both Heroes agree it no longer describes them, and mark a Bond; use any relevant Party Improvement; or progress a Project Clock. Each Hero can take Camp Actions equal to the number of Party Improvements.' },
195:       { Id: 'g-push-yourself', Name: 'Push Yourself', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When more than one of your Skill Tags applies to a roll, mark one Condition to add a second +1 on top of your declared Skill Tag’s own +1.' },
196:       { Id: 'g-set-out', Name: 'Set Out', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Gathering the party and venturing forth on the next leg of an Adventure — Choose your Loadout, then either simply arrive at a safe destination or Undertake a Perilous Journey through Scout Ahead and Venture Forth. Formerly named "Undertake a Journey."' },
197:       { Id: 'g-opposition-clock', Name: 'Opposition Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The most common Clock — a Success track and a Failure track, both starting at 0 Headway. Risking 1-3 Headway before a roll: a 10+ adds the risked Headway to Success, a 7-9 adds it to both, a 6- adds it to Failure.' },
198:       { Id: 'g-threat-clock', Name: 'Threat Clock', Aliases: ['Threat Clocks'], Definition: 'A player-facing Clock for a brewing danger the Heroes have learned of — a Name, description, Goal, Skill Tags, and Developments (roughly one per segment), sized 2-4 for a nearby Threat, 4-6 regional, 7+ realm-spanning. A GM may promote one to the campaign\'s Quest Board. Advances by the GM\'s own hand, often at Make Camp — this app doesn\'t advance a neglected Threat on its own.' },
199:       { Id: 'g-project-clock', Name: 'Project Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Hero\'s own downtime pursuit — building, crafting, enchanting, researching, and the like. Give it a name, description, and Goal; progress it by rolling + an appropriate ability and reporting the tier (10+: 3 segments, 7-9: 2, 6-: 1), the same way Enjoy Downtime\'s Advance and a Camp Action already work.' },
200:       { Id: 'g-development', Name: 'Development', Aliases: ['Developments'], Definition: 'A planned consequence tied to one segment of a Threat Clock, triggered whenever it best serves the pacing rather than strictly in order — early Developments introduce the Threat lightly, later ones raise the stakes.' },
201:       { Id: 'g-headway', Name: 'Headway', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The amount (1-3) a Hero risks before rolling to progress an Opposition Clock — gained by the Heroes on a 10+, by both sides on a 7-9, or by the opposition alone on a 6-.' },
202:       { Id: 'g-villain', Name: 'Villain', Aliases: ['Villains'], Definition: 'The antagonist driving an Adventure’s conflict — a monster, person, or anomaly with a Goal, a Scar, Skill Tags, Resources, Powers, Attacks, Resistances and Vulnerabilities, and Status Limits. A Villain doesn’t need to be killed or even defeated to conclude an Adventure — their Goal only needs to be thwarted.' },
203:       { Id: 'g-npc', Name: 'NPC', Aliases: ['NPCs', 'Non-Player Character'], Definition: 'A supporting-cast character with a Type (their function to you as a GM — Meddler, Minion, Gossip, Ally, Guard, Opportunist, Skeptic, Victim, or Witness), a Goal, and Skill Tags. A Combatant NPC gets Status Limits, same as an Enemy.' },
204:       { Id: 'g-location', Name: 'Location', Aliases: ['Locations'], Definition: 'A place the Heroes are expected to spend time during an Adventure — 3 Aspects the Heroes can interact with, plus a Location Type (Nexus, Deathtrap, Lair, Citadel, Lab, Archive, Labyrinth, Gaol, or Wilds) describing its purpose.' },
205:       { Id: 'g-party-motif', Name: 'Party Motif', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The Motif the whole Party shares: why you travel together. It holds two Party Skill Tags and two Party Flaw Tags, and a Party Quest. Each Party Tag works for a single Hero Roll, then refreshes when the Party Makes Camp; invoking one marks Rapport.' },
206:       { Id: 'g-party-improvement', Name: 'Party Improvement', Aliases: ['Party Improvements'], Definition: 'An improvement the whole Party gains — one at creation, and more through Progress the Party. Each Hero may take as many Camp Actions as the Party has Party Improvements.' },

    ],
    glossary: [
      { Id: 'g-condition', Name: 'Condition', Aliases: ['Conditions'], Definition: 'A marked penalty tied to one of your five Virtues — Exhausted (Might), Afraid (Mettle), Guilty (Heart), Angry (Wit), Insecure (Guile). When you mark a Condition, you gain an associated Bane on any relevant roll until you clear it. Marking a Condition when all five are already marked means you Crumble.' },
      { Id: 'g-hero-roll', Name: 'Hero Roll', Aliases: ['Hero Rolls'], Definition: 'Roll 2d6 and add the relevant Virtue. Add +1 for one relevant Skill Tag and −1 for every relevant Flaw Tag. You may Push Yourself once per roll: mark a Condition and add +1 for a second relevant Skill Tag. The final modifier cannot exceed +3 or fall below −3. After determining the modifier, apply Advantage or Disadvantage from your Boons and Banes.' },
      { Id: 'g-misfortune', Name: 'Misfortune', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The GM’s currency. At the beginning of a Session, if the GM has none, they gain 1. Whenever a Hero rolls 6-, in or out of Combat, the GM gains 1. The GM spends it 1 for 1 to make a Hard Move at any time, including immediately, and some GM and Enemy Moves cost Misfortune too. It carries over between Sessions and resets to 1 when an Adventure concludes.' },
      { Id: 'g-hard-move', Name: 'Hard Move', Aliases: ['Hard Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that gives the Heroes no time to react: it afflicts them with a tangible penalty, in the fiction or directly (marking Strain or a Condition), and the stakes meaningfully change. The GM must spend a Misfortune to make one.' },
      { Id: 'g-soft-move', Name: 'Soft Move', Aliases: ['Soft Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that threatens danger or pushes the Heroes toward a choice, while leaving them time to stop or divert it — often a setup ending in “What do you do?” A Soft Move can telegraph a later Hard Move.' },
      { Id: 'g-rapport', Name: 'Rapport', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A party-wide track marked when a move tells you to "mark Rapport." Filling it clears the track and raises Party Level by 1 — see Improvement. Rapport can also be spent directly as Aid — see Aid.' },
      { Id: 'g-work-together', Name: 'Work Together', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When any number of Heroes want to work as a group, the GM may ask for the Party to make a single Hero Roll to determine the outcome of a Move where the Party is acting as one. Each Hero may contribute one relevant Skill Tag, and any or all of the Party Tags may be used if they are relevant. All Hero’s Flaw Tags may affect the roll as well, and the outcome affects the entire group.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-quest', Name: 'Party Quest', Aliases: ['Party Quests'], Definition: 'What your group all must seek together — your reason for traveling as one rather than individuals. It creates a path forward leading into Adventures and drives the story. Four varieties help define it: Vision (how the Party wants to change their world), Covenant (a binding vow or shared ideology), Shield (a realm or population to defend), or Expedition (a mystery or truth to uncover).' },
      { Id: 'g-motif', Name: 'Motif', Aliases: ['Motifs'], Definition: 'One of the three core aspects of your Hero — each a bucket for its own Skill Tags, Flaw Tags, a Potential track, and a Quest. You choose three Motifs at creation (from the thirteen suggested, or your own) and may rename any of them to fit your character.' },
      { Id: 'g-skill-tag', Name: 'Skill Tag', Aliases: ['Skill Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing something your Hero is good at. Declare a relevant Skill Tag before a roll to add +1; if more than one applies you may Push Yourself, mark a Condition, and add another +1.' },
      { Id: 'g-flaw-tag', Name: 'Flaw Tag', Aliases: ['Flaw Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing a limit or weakness. A relevant Flaw Tag gives -1 to the roll, and acting on it marks Potential on that Motif whether the roll succeeds or fails.' },
      { Id: 'g-quest', Name: 'Quest', Aliases: ['Quests'], Definition: 'A short, player-written goal hanging off one Motif, tracked with three Act Breaks and three Forsakes. Three Act Breaks complete it; three Forsakes abandon it.' },
      { Id: 'g-potential', Name: 'Potential', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A track on each Motif, marked when a move tells you to "mark Potential" (or when you act on a Flaw Tag). Filling a Motif’s track clears it, raises Level by 1, and lets you add a Skill Tag, add or remove a Flaw Tag, or gain a Hero Improvement — see Improvement.' },
      { Id: 'g-improvement', Name: 'Improvement', Aliases: ['Improvements', 'Improvement Tree', 'Hero Improvement'], Definition: 'A permanent pick taken off one of 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat, 14 Narrative) when a full Motif Potential track clears. Each tree is its own small prerequisite chain: take a tree’s Starting Improvement any time, or any other Improvement on that tree once you already hold one it connects to. Each Improvement can only be taken once. Party Improvements are named in the rules the same way but have no authored trees yet.' },
      { Id: 'g-hold', Name: 'Hold', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A pool of uses granted by a Move on a strong hit and spent one at a time until it runs out. Assess the Situation and Discern the Truth grant it; spend it to refresh a piece of Gear, clear a Condition, mark a Bond, or mark Potential.' },
      { Id: 'g-load', Name: 'Load', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How much you can carry. Each Item has a Load cost (0, 1, or 2); your total carried Load is capped by your Light/Normal/Heavy tier.' },
      { Id: 'g-bond', Name: 'Bond', Aliases: ['Bonds', 'Mark Bond', 'Bond Track', 'Bond Level'], Definition: 'How deeply a Connection between two Heroes runs, measured on its Bond Track. Mark 1 Bond when your Connection Tag meaningfully influences an important choice, creates a significant complication, or helps the two of you overcome a great obstacle together (once per Connection per scene), or when a move tells you to "mark Bond". At 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the Bond Track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement. Either Hero may spend a Bond at any time to influence the other. Marking Bond and Forging go through a propose/accept/reject handshake between the two players; spending Bond applies immediately.' },
      { Id: 'g-connection', Name: 'Connection', Aliases: ['Connections', 'Connection Tag', 'Connection Tags'], Definition: "Each pair of Heroes has one Connection, with a Connection Tag the two agree on that describes where their relationship stands now — pick one of the ruleset's examples or write your own. Bond is marked on it; at 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement." },
      { Id: 'g-status', Name: 'Status', Aliases: ['Statuses'], Definition: 'A named, lasting injury held in one of three severity slots — Minor (×3), Major (×2), or Severe (×1). Only the highest-severity Status you hold ever penalizes a roll: Minor is −1, Major is Disadvantage, Severe means rolling 1d6 instead of 2d6. Distinct from Strain (a short-term track that clears at the end of a scene) and from a Condition (always one of the five Virtue-linked penalties). Reduced by Recuperating, or downgraded a severity when your Healing Track fills.' },
      { Id: 'g-strain', Name: 'Strain', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-box short-term harm track that clears completely at the end of the scene or Combat in which it was taken. Mark the box equal to an incoming amount, or the next unmarked box to its right. Resist an incoming amount by rolling + a Virtue to reduce it, or by choosing to take a Status instead (which absorbs a flat 2/4/6 by severity). Armor negates Strain entirely, up to its own limit.' },
      { Id: 'g-healing-track', Name: 'Healing Track', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-segment track advanced by Recuperating (+Mettle: 3/2/1 segments by tier). When it fills, every Status you hold drops one severity (renamed to reflect the improvement, where a slot is free at the lower severity) and the track clears, carrying any remaining segments onto the fresh one.' },
      { Id: 'g-boon', Name: 'Boon', Aliases: ['Boons'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working in your favor — cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Banes on a roll: more relevant Boons than Banes gives Advantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-bane', Name: 'Bane', Aliases: ['Banes'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working against you — cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Boons on a roll: more relevant Banes than Boons gives Disadvantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-immobilized', Name: 'Immobilized', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A special Bane representing anything that prevents voluntary movement: grappling, paralysis, restraints, or binding magic. While Immobilized your Speed is 0 and you cannot move voluntarily, Maneuver, or Shift, but you may take other actions and forced movement can still move you. A Boon may cancel its effect on a roll but does not restore your movement. It ends when its fictional cause disappears or when someone successfully uses Break.' },
      { Id: 'g-crumble', Name: 'Crumble', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When you need to mark a Condition but all of them are already marked, you Crumble: you lose consciousness, flee, or otherwise must leave the scene. Say how, then clear one Condition immediately, and discuss with the GM how and when you’ll return. If you Crumble in Combat, you can only take actions that result in you fleeing or avoiding the action.' },
      { Id: 'g-subdued', Name: 'Subdued', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When a Hero must mark Strain but has no Strain box and does not prevent the Strain by taking a Status or using Armor, they are Subdued: they cannot continue the conflict, and the player and GM describe how they are removed from immediate danger — knocked unconscious, pinned, captured, separated, or forced to retreat. Subdual does not kill a Hero unless the player agrees that death is the appropriate outcome; what else happens is left to the table. An Enemy is Subdued when no legal Strain box remains (a Minion by any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain), and the Hero who subdued it and the fiction decide whether it is unconscious, captured, routed, or killed.' },
      { Id: 'g-scar', Name: 'Scar', Aliases: ['Scars'], Definition: 'A near-permanent consequence a Hero can carry — a lost limb, a lingering nightmare, an unwanted transformation. The old Subdued-triggered choice that used to grant one (Take a Scar / Risk Death / Blaze of Glory) has been retired with no stated replacement; Scars themselves stay on the sheet as free text for whenever the table narrates one.' },
      { Id: 'g-guard', Name: 'Guard', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Reduces the Strain inflicted on an Enemy by its value — Guard 1 by 1, Guard 2 by 2 — but never below 1 Strain, and it doesn’t reduce Conditions or effects inflicted instead of Strain. Pierce ignores it. Guard should be visible in the fiction: a shield, a stone shell, a spectral barrier, impossible speed.' },
      { Id: 'g-pierce', Name: 'Pierce', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Gambit: ignore the Enemy’s Guard for this Move. See Guard.' },
      { Id: 'g-threat', Name: 'Threat', Aliases: ['Threat Level'], Definition: 'How many Heroes an Enemy is expected to occupy: ½ for a Minion, 1 Standard, 2 Elite, 4 Legendary. Add every Enemy’s Threat and divide by the number of Heroes — Easy .5, Medium .75, Hard 1, Deadly 1.25, Very Deadly 1.5 or more. It is only a starting estimate.' },
      { Id: 'g-enemy-profile', Name: 'Enemy Profile', Aliases: ['Enemy Profiles', 'Minion', 'Minions', 'Elite', 'Legendary'], Definition: 'How much of a fight an Enemy is, which sets its defaults for Strain, Status slots and Conditions. A Minion (Threat ½) is weak alone but dangerous in groups, and any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain Subdues it; a Standard Enemy (Threat 1) can take on one Hero; an Elite (Threat 2) can take on two at once; a Legendary Enemy (Threat 4) fights the whole party, taking a turn after every Hero’s turn. See Threat.' },
      { Id: 'g-last-stand', Name: 'Last Stand', Aliases: ['Bloodied'], Definition: 'A Legendary Enemy fights in three phases — Opening, Bloodied, then Last Stand (N) — each a five-box Strain track unless its stat block says otherwise. When a phase can’t mark incoming Strain, it ends and the rest of that Strain is discarded. It loses at most one phase between its own activations. Last Stand (N) clears the N highest-numbered marked boxes, which become its final capacity; when it can’t mark Strain in Last Stand, it is Subdued.' },
      { Id: 'g-range', Name: 'Range', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How far apart two combatants are: Melee, Close, Far, Very Far, or Out of Range. Maneuver and Shift move you between bands; Engage at Range and Engage in Melee each only work at their own band.' },
      { Id: 'g-aid', Name: 'Aid', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Spend 1 Rapport to give another Hero +1 on a roll, even after the dice are already rolled. You can Aid the same roll once per teammate, and Aid from multiple teammates stacks. Adding +1 this way cannot exceed +3 total on the roll.' },
      { Id: 'g-wealth', Name: 'Wealth', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet. Named sinks: spend 1 to roll Follow a Lead with Advantage, or during Enjoy Downtime to Rest, Carouse, Acquire, or Train.' },
      { Id: 'g-treasure', Name: 'Treasure', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet like Wealth. Ruleset-V0.6.md names no Wealth-distinct sink for Treasure any more — Carouse spends Wealth now — so it stays a freely adjusted resource with no automated hook.' },
      { Id: 'g-advantage', Name: 'Advantage', Aliases: ['Disadvantage'], Definition: 'Roll 3d6 and keep the best two (Advantage) or worst two (Disadvantage) instead of the usual 2d6 — decided by comparing your Boons and Banes relevant to the roll: more Boons is Advantage, more Banes is Disadvantage, a tie (including none of either) is Normal. A Major Status is a separate source of Disadvantage the ruleset doesn’t say how to combine with a Boon/Bane-driven one — both are shown, and the table resolves it. Double Disadvantage (from Repeated Attacks) is the worst possible roll: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two.' },
      { Id: 'g-double-disadvantage', Name: 'Double Disadvantage', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The worst possible roll a Hero can make, arising from Repeated Attacks: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two. This is the only rule that creates Double Disadvantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-repeated-attacks', Name: 'Repeated Attacks', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Whenever a Hero spends AP on a Move that can inflict Strain, count how many such Moves they have used since their AP last refreshed. Work out Advantage or Disadvantage from Boons and Banes as normal, then worsen the roll one step for each previous Strain-inflicting Move, as far as Double Disadvantage. A Move counts once however many creatures it targets, and a Reaction counts if it costs AP and can inflict Strain.' },
      { Id: 'g-prepare', Name: 'Prepare', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Combat Move: your maximum AP becomes 4 during your next turn. Prepare does not stack with itself, and after that turn ends your maximum returns to normal.' },
      { Id: 'g-combat-goal', Name: 'Combat Goal', Aliases: ['Combat Goals'], Definition: 'The objective that must be achieved to end Combat, agreed on by the GM and Heroes when entering the Combat system. Examples include defeating the opposition, rescuing a prisoner, recovering an item, crossing a bridge, or escaping an area. If the Heroes initiate Combat and all share the goal, they mark 1 Rapport.' },
      { Id: 'g-defiant-goal', Name: 'Defiant Goal', Aliases: ['Defiant Goals'], Definition: 'An alternative objective a minority of Heroes may declare during Combat if they disagree with the main Combat Goal. Achieving a Defiant Goal allows only those Heroes to leave Combat. Combat ends for everyone only if the table agrees the Defiant Goal has superseded the main Goal.' },
      { Id: 'g-consequence', Name: 'Consequence', Aliases: ['Burdened', 'Compromised', 'Delayed', 'Depleted', 'Exposed', 'Consequences'], Definition: 'One of five named outcomes on Invoke Expertise and Take a Risk: Burdened (a worse outcome, hard choice, or price to pay), Compromised (the situation escalates), Delayed (you take too long; things change meaningfully), Depleted (expend a resource or break a useful item), or Exposed (draw unwanted attention or leave a traceable trail). Replaces the old Attrition/Detection/Danger/Delay/Sacrifice vocabulary.' },
      { Id: 'g-camp-asset', Name: 'Camp Asset', Aliases: ['Camp Assets'], Definition: 'A magic item the party is afforded at creation to help them set up camp, leveling up through Tiers as the party progresses. Pick one from the library, or write your own on the spot.' },
      { Id: 'g-camp-action', Name: 'Camp Action', Aliases: ['Camp Actions'], Definition: 'One of the things each Hero may do at Make Camp: rewrite or update one of your Skill or Flaw Tags for the Party Motif, or for one of your Motifs; rewrite your Connection Tag, if both Heroes agree it no longer describes them, and mark a Bond; use any relevant Party Improvement; or progress a Project Clock. Each Hero can take Camp Actions equal to the number of Party Improvements.' },
      { Id: 'g-push-yourself', Name: 'Push Yourself', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When more than one of your Skill Tags applies to a roll, mark one Condition to add a second +1 on top of your declared Skill Tag’s own +1.' },
      { Id: 'g-set-out', Name: 'Set Out', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Gathering the party and venturing forth on the next leg of an Adventure — Choose your Loadout, then either simply arrive at a safe destination or Undertake a Perilous Journey through Scout Ahead and Venture Forth. Formerly named "Undertake a Journey."' },
      { Id: 'g-opposition-clock', Name: 'Opposition Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The most common Clock — a Success track and a Failure track, both starting at 0 Headway. Risking 1-3 Headway before a roll: a 10+ adds the risked Headway to Success, a 7-9 adds it to both, a 6- adds it to Failure.' },
      { Id: 'g-threat-clock', Name: 'Threat Clock', Aliases: ['Threat Clocks'], Definition: 'A player-facing Clock for a brewing danger the Heroes have learned of — a Name, description, Goal, Skill Tags, and Developments (roughly one per segment), sized 2-4 for a nearby Threat, 4-6 regional, 7+ realm-spanning. A GM may promote one to the campaign\'s Quest Board. Advances by the GM\'s own hand, often at Make Camp — this app doesn\'t advance a neglected Threat on its own.' },
      { Id: 'g-project-clock', Name: 'Project Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Hero\'s own downtime pursuit — building, crafting, enchanting, researching, and the like. Give it a name, description, and Goal; progress it by rolling + an appropriate ability and reporting the tier (10+: 3 segments, 7-9: 2, 6-: 1), the same way Enjoy Downtime\'s Advance and a Camp Action already work.' },
      { Id: 'g-development', Name: 'Development', Aliases: ['Developments'], Definition: 'A planned consequence tied to one segment of a Threat Clock, triggered whenever it best serves the pacing rather than strictly in order — early Developments introduce the Threat lightly, later ones raise the stakes.' },
      { Id: 'g-headway', Name: 'Headway', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The amount (1-3) a Hero risks before rolling to progress an Opposition Clock — gained by the Heroes on a 10+, by both sides on a 7-9, or by the opposition alone on a 6-.' },
      { Id: 'g-villain', Name: 'Villain', Aliases: ['Villains'], Definition: 'The antagonist driving an Adventure’s conflict — a monster, person, or anomaly with a Goal, a Scar, Skill Tags, Resources, Powers, Attacks, Resistances and Vulnerabilities, and Status Limits. A Villain doesn’t need to be killed or even defeated to conclude an Adventure — their Goal only needs to be thwarted.' },
      { Id: 'g-npc', Name: 'NPC', Aliases: ['NPCs', 'Non-Player Character'], Definition: 'A supporting-cast character with a Type (their function to you as a GM — Meddler, Minion, Gossip, Ally, Guard, Opportunist, Skeptic, Victim, or Witness), a Goal, and Skill Tags. A Combatant NPC gets Status Limits, same as an Enemy.' },
      { Id: 'g-location', Name: 'Location', Aliases: ['Locations'], Definition: 'A place the Heroes are expected to spend time during an Adventure — 3 Aspects the Heroes can interact with, plus a Location Type (Nexus, Deathtrap, Lair, Citadel, Lab, Archive, Labyrinth, Gaol, or Wilds) describing its purpose.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-motif', Name: 'Party Motif', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The Motif the whole Party shares: why you travel together. It holds two Party Skill Tags and two Party Flaw Tags, and a Party Quest. Each Party Tag works for a single Hero Roll, then refreshes when the Party Makes Camp; invoking one marks Rapport.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-improvement', Name: 'Party Improvement', Aliases: ['Party Improvements'], Definition: 'An improvement the whole Party gains — one at creation, and more through Progress the Party. Each Hero may take as many Camp Actions as the Party has Party Improvements.' },
    ],

## Objective
- Resolve a data bug where Basic Move `VirtueId` values in `seedLibrary.ts` disagree with their corresponding headings in `Ruleset-V0.6.md`. Write a validation test in `seedLibrary.test.ts` that parses the ruleset chapter on Basic Moves and cross-references it against the seed data, then fix the seed file so it conforms and passes.

## Important Details
- Constraints: Edit ONLY `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.ts` and `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.test.ts`. Do not commit. Run `cd packages/shared && npx vitest run` upon completion.
- Ruleset path: `Planning Docs/Ruleset-V0.6.md` (contains a space; may have LF or CRLF line endings).
- Basic Moves parsing scope: Locate chapter starting with `## Basic Moves` up to the next top-level heading (`^# `).
- Heading patterns to parse: `## Move Name (Virtue)`, `## Move Name \-(Virtue)`, `## Move Name (Virtue1/Virtue2)`, or `## Move Name (Any)` (strip trailing spaces).
- Validation logic: Exactly one Virtue in parentheses → set `VirtueId` to that Virtue's seeded Id. Two Virtues or `Any` → keep `VirtueId` as `null`.
- Test requirement: New file `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.test.ts` must FAIL if the seed fix is reverted while tests remain. Every parsed heading must have a corresponding seeded Move.

## Work State
### Completed
- Explored repo directory structure and confirmed `Planning Docs/Ruleset-V0.6.md` location.
- Read `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.ts` (initial `IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS` and partial `MOVES` array).
- Read `packages/shared/src/types.ts` to understand `Move`, `Virtue`, and `VirtueKey` type shapes.
- Executed `grep` for `^## ` headings in `Planning Docs` to identify section boundaries in the ruleset.

### Active
- Analyzing grep output and planning the regex/parser for the `## Basic Moves` chapter boundaries.
- Need to extract the exact mapping of Move names to Virtue constraints from the ruleset before drafting the test assertions.

### Blocked
- None currently, but original grep result was truncated; full `## Basic Moves` chapter context is required next.

## Next Move
1. Read the full `## Basic Moves` section of `Planning Docs/Ruleset-V0.6.md` using a reliable reader/extractor to capture all Move headings and their Virtue parentheses.
2. Create `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.test.ts` implementing ruleset parsing, cross-referencing against `seedLibrary.ts`, and asserting `VirtueId` correctness.
3. Apply minimal fixes to `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.ts` based on test failures.
4. Run `cd packages/shared && npx vitest run` and verify the entire suite passes.

## Relevant Files
- `Planning Docs/Ruleset-V0.6.md`: Canonical ruleset defining Basic Moves and their Virtue requirements; source of truth for the test.
- `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.ts`: Target file containing the `MOVES` array with `VirtueId` values that must be corrected.
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`: Defines `Move`, `Virtue`, and `VirtueKey` shapes used by the seed data and test logic.
- `packages/shared/src/seedLibrary.test.ts`: New file to be created for validation and regression prevention.
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.
